column2: `parse_plan_commands` in `plan_quality.py` recognizes `### new:` and `### updated:` for `pending_updated` and section-reset logic, but not `### may_update:`. a conditional section using `### may_update:` with `- adds flag: --new-flag` will not emit an `updated_flag` row, so plan validation can report an unknown flag even though the same content under `### updated:` would pass.

the gate b revise-waterfall hard rule in `_compose_revise_prompt` only requires preserving `### new:`, `### updated:`, or `### rewritten:` headings. it does not forbid converting `### may_update:` into a firm heading. after plan review, revise-waterfall may rewrite `### may_update:` as `### updated:` while `_heading_count` still passes; `/implement` coverage then treats the path as firm and `warn_plan_files_untouched` can fire on a correct conditional skip.

python/plan_quality.py:621-681 [scope-reduction] parse_plan_commands may_update/- adds flag: parity is not on the reported bug path the #4865 false positive was a conditional file skip with no `- adds flag:` rows; today ### may_update: clears pending_updated like any other non-updated heading, which does not break that scenario.. scenario: ~40 lines of parser + golden-test churn for a path no existing report needs; increases blast radius without fixing the observed warn.

skills/design/scripts/design-step3b-entry.sh:116-118,175-177; skills/design/scripts/design-step3b-entry.md:16 new may_update plan heading is missing from the step 3b architecture-diagram classifier. scenario: after the plan updates /design to emit ### may_update:, a conditional docs-only plan has no recognized file heading here, so step 3b treats it as heading-free and forces diagram_required=true instead of preserving the existing no-architectural-change skip behavior
